text:
Maya R: quick dump from today — p95 spike on route /chat/streaming between 11:03 and 11:10. profiler shows repeated kernel handoffs when microbatch size == 1
Maya R: looks like we hit fallback path for fused-attn on longer prefix lengths, so each token incurs extra memcpy
Liam C: can you paste the trace?
Maya R: stack: 
```
GPU kernel: attn_fused_v2 -> attn_unfused_fallback -> kv_write -> memcpy_sync
latency samples: 120ms -> 210ms -> 340ms
```
Anika S: hmm KV cache misses look high for that traffic segment? prefix hit-rate dropped to 63%
Maya R: yes — correlated with a tiny percent of requests that have long system prompts. batcher keeps them separate and microbatch==1 ends up choosing slower kernel
Frank P: so two knobs: prefer kernel selection by estimated seq_len OR bias batch formation to combine long-prefix requests together so fused kernel stays viable
Liam C: we should also consider token-budget gating per route/tier — if a route is latency-sensitive (gold tier) we keep token_budget low so it prefers fast path (even if cost rises)
Anika S: proposal: "latency-slotter" heuristic — at enqueue time compute slot = min(max_slots, ceil(seq_len / slot_window)) then allow dynamic token_budget_by_slot and route_priority override
Maya R: sketch config: 
```
queue_policy: slotter_v1
slot_window: 64
max_slots: 4
token_budget_by_slot:
  "1": 64
  "2": 48
  "3": 32
  "4": 16
route_overrides:
  "/chat/streaming": { "tier": "gold", "min_budget": 32 }
```
Frank P: that looks reasonable. slot 1 gets bigger budget -> can form larger microbatches -> fused kernel chosen. slot 4 tiny budget avoids long-running tokens on tail-sensitive routes
Liam C: how do we route kernel selection? we need lightweight estimator on worker so we don't fetch full model meta each request
Maya R: use cheap heuristic: if avg_seq_len_estimate <= slot_window*slot we set preferred_kernel=fused, else unfused. fallback remains if fused not available
dev-bot: perf-check triggered: run-profiler --route "/chat/streaming" --window 11:00-11:20 --buckets seq_len,kv-hit-rate
Anika S: I ran that locally — results: after applying slotter sim (offline) p95 drops from 360ms -> 190ms on the sample trace; throughput delta +8%
Liam C: nice. any regressions? memory usage when forcing fused?
Maya R: small bump in GPU mem (~120MB) on worst-case but within Dedicated limits. bigger risk is starvation of low-tier bursty routes if we greedily pack long-prefix into large microbatches
Frank P: suggest adding per-tier fairness gate: max_tokens_reserved_per_tier and an eviction policy that demotes low-tier when SLO violation detected
Anika S: also KV behavior — we need to prefetch KV for slot >1 candidates. current prefetch only triggers when batch size >=4 which is too conservative
Maya R: suggested prefetch rule: if slot_estimate >=2 OR seq_len_estimate > 128 then prefetch KV async on enqueue; config snippet: 
```
prefetch:
  min_slot: 2
  async: true
  timeout_ms: 20
```
Liam C: testing plan: canary on region us-west2, route /chat/streaming, 5% traffic, collect p95, kv-hit-rate, kernel_switch_rate, gpu_mem. rollback if p95 rises >5% or kernel_switch_rate increases
Frank P: add observability: metric route.slot_distribution, route.kernel_prefers, route.kv_prefetchs_success
Maya R: action items:
- Anika: implement slotter_v1 queue policy + prefetch rule (PR)
- Liam: add lightweight kernel estimator on worker + metrics (PR)
- Frank: configure canary + dashboards + alarms
- Maya: run offline sims vs last 7 days traces and push config to canary
Liam C: ETA?
Anika S: PR today for policy, test tomorrow
Frank P: canary by Friday EOD
Maya R: if canary looks good we'll roll to Dedicated stable lanes next week. thanks! :thumbsup:
